title: Is the Yale Global Tic Severity Scale a valid tool for parent-reported assessment in the paediatric population? A prospective observational study in Taiwan
review_scope: Historical study selected by October 27 informant-agreement question, not newly published evidence
population: Regularly followed pediatric Tourette patients at one Taiwan clinic; final mean age 8.8 years (SD 2.97). Adult, ASD/communication-specific and chronic motor/vocal-only validation not established.
intervention: No randomized intervention; observational association between repeated form completion and score differences
comparator: Parent versus pediatric fellow scores/category; clinician reference is not independent biological truth. Both masked to other score, not necessarily independent information.
instrument: Author-translated revised traditional Chinese online YGTSS form; exact identity with 2018 YGTSS-R not verified. Figure 1 is partial illustration.
timing: Parents encouraged to complete day before visit, fellows at visit; Results simultaneous wording conflicts with explicit nonsimultaneous limitation. Same-visit pairing retained.
outcomes: Entire score and motor/vocal/combined tic and separate impairment differences; binary clinician-reference discrimination with exact score endpoint and handling value 20 unresolved
follow_up: June 2018–April 2019 collection with repeated outpatient assessments; not prospective treatment efficacy or clinical improvement
analysis_methods: Reported GEE accounts for participant clustering in repeated differences; logistic GEE described for discrimination. No models refitted.
aggregate_reconciliation: 507/636 sensitivity and 752/819 specificity reproduce printed rounding; 196/1455 discordant assessments, not distinct people. Mean-absolute conditional triangle bounds .01–4.81 include reported entire 4.15, so component nonadditivity is not automatically an error.
negative_and_conflicting_evidence: No numerical correlation coefficient, ICC, agreement limits or prespecified equivalence margin identified in inspected report
Fourth-assessment nonsignificance is not equivalence; repeated exposure not randomized training
Mild<20 versus moderate/severe>20 leaves 20 undefined; no cutoff repair or inferred boundary counts
Methods absolute differences versus subtraction wording unresolved, so no directional parent bias inferred
Simultaneous Results wording contradicted by timing/limitations
Convenience sampling and partial report pairing limit generalization
attrition_missingness: 67 enrollees absent paired analysis; 1,901 parent reports unpaired; 67 of 1,522 fellow evaluations unpaired, numerically the same 67 but a different unit. Not established retention or missing-patient counts.
uncertainty: No de novo cluster-naive intervals, score-sign reconstruction, per-repetition retention or patient-level agreement estimate. Exact difference coding and dichotomized score definition unresolved.
adverse_events: Not intervention safety evidence; no absence-of-risk inference
risk_of_bias: Selected familiar clinic families and few newly diagnosed patients
Convenience fellow assessment and incomplete pairing
Shared symptom information despite masked numeric scores
Unadjusted important severity/duration characteristics and repeated-visit selection
Variable parent/fellow assessment; limited subgroup eligibility reporting
funding_conflicts: No specific research grant declared; competing interests none declared, not independent comprehensive verification
claim_supported: Promising parent-report discrimination against clinician categories and observational repeated-assessment association in this clinic
retrieval_status: Official EuropePMC XML inspected transiently; reviewer visually checked Figures1–2 from official archive. Publisher 403. No full paper, images or participant narratives retained.
correction_retraction_check: No linked PubMed notice or notice in bounded exact DOI search; not exhaustive clearance
reviewer: AI-assisted aggregate/methods audit with independent source/arithmetic review, not clinical peer review
next_verification_task: Close fixed audit absent clarifications. Next audit Wang et al. (2026), PMID 42680906, public aggregate transdiagnostic versus chronic-tic-specific gene evidence, overlap/ascertainment, multiplicity and replication; no individual variants or therapeutic-target inference.
